evidence.reason: In the no-process.json path, when `_show_scope` reports `LoadState` as `not-found`, the code skips the ownership check and still unconditionally runs `systemctl --user stop derived_unit`. Since the unit name is derived only from the run ID and different state directories do not share the run-directory lock, a colliding scope created between the show and the stop could be stopped even though this run never owned it. The smallest compatible fix is to skip the stop when the pre-stop query proves the scope absent; the later stopped verification cannot undo an already-issued stop. Binding scope names to the run directory is additional hardening rather than a prerequisite for the minimal fix.
